P1.evidence: No setter notes were read back. The rep referenced the application generically — 'I did see your application' — and only mentioned Sophia twenty minutes in, to ask whether a link had been checked. Nothing was fed back that would make the prospect feel seen. Frame remains three-part. Agreement asked and given. The open question was folded into the frame rather than asked as its own question, and the prospect self-started, so P1d only partly credits.

P2.evidence: The injury work was outstanding and the best single stretch of discovery in the batch — the 1-to-10 scale asked twice, producing a layered answer (7 general, 8-9 for the elbow on pushing and pulling, and a self-assessed 10 for the compounding compensation chain from ankle to knee to hip to lower back). Diet was asked and produced a blunt 'Terrible' plus the structural cause, three restaurant meetings a day around client schedules. Everything else is thin. Age, height and weight were never established at all — for a prospect whose primary goal is fat loss, there is no baseline to measure against, and 'over 40' is all we know. Health conditions were never asked. Sleep was never mentioned. Energy was inferred rather than asked; the rep later asserted 'your energy is quite on the low end' having never posed the question. Work was established as heavy travel and sales but the industry and role were never pinned down, which matters for the ICP.

P3.evidence: The first half ran well. The definition question was specific — 'is it a fact of strength? Is it fat storage or what sort of definition you need to work on the most?' — and the can't-do-now check surfaced real material: gassing out when sparring, and getting winded tying his shoes. The bridge produced the most valuable line on the call: 'the rest of my life is going well... This is the one area where I've just accepted, I continue to make excuses for myself.' Then it stopped. There is no future-pacing anywhere in 51 minutes — never 'imagine six months from now', never 'what would that do for you'. And nobody else exists in this call: no partner, no children, no friends, nothing about who else is affected, because P3f was never asked. The result is a why built entirely on self-image, which is real but thin, and when the price landed there was nothing outside himself to weigh it against.

P4.evidence: The need question ran and landed — 'What else do you feel like that's what I need in order to actually get to the outcome instead of staying the same?' — and the prospect named the gap repeatedly in his own words across the call: 'I need direction when it comes to working out', 'I need that additional push', 'I continue to make excuses for myself'. But past attempts were never explored: what he has tried, what happened, why it stopped. And P4f was never asked, which is the costly one. This prospect later raised the DIY alternative himself as the reason to hesitate — 'I could go online and say, hey, show me some kettlebell workouts, tell me what to eat' — and because the root cause was never established, the rep had nothing to answer it with and did not try.

P5.evidence: The settle question ran, phrased against the prospect's own 5-out-of-10 self-rating: 'you mentioned if you keep going the same way, it's okay, it's not terrible... If you already feel like that, why don't you just stay the same?' That worked, producing 'I don't want to be mediocre.' The why-not follow-up ran too and drew out the excuse-making admission. What is missing is any concrete cost of inaction — no two-year picture, no version of what the compensation chain looks like at 50, despite the prospect having handed over an injury cascade he himself rated 10 out of 10 for cumulative damage. The commitment ask, 'are you also ready to actually give up on the excuses?', is close to a line in the sand but is about attitude rather than action.

P6.evidence: The pre-price check was asked — 'do you feel like, yeah, outside of the price, it is something I see myself doing?' — but the answer was a single word, 'Right', which is not a clear yes, and the rep proceeded anyway. The go-all-in question was never asked in its proper form. P6c fails on sequencing too: a price range was given at roughly the twenty-three minute mark, before goals were complete, and the rep said so out loud at the time — 'we haven't gone over your complete goals yet so it's hard to say'. He knew he was out of order and did it anyway because the prospect asked.

P11.evidence: No agreement, so nothing downstream was reachable. Worth noting the weaker fallback here compared with other calls in this batch: no follow-up meeting was booked at all, only a vague 'I'll follow up in like a week or two'.

objection_plays.detail: The best OA handling in the batch, though still incomplete. Ran: the fit-versus-money isolation ('is this a fit for me, or is that more because of the money aspect?'), the competing-options question ('what other options are you thinking about?'), a strong attack on the open-ended timeline ('if you give yourself another month, why not give yourself another two, another three? Why not actually make that decision?'), and the residual-objection check ('would there still be an objection that's holding you back from making a decision?'). It produced a real commitment to a couple of weeks. Missing: 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', 'what makes you feel it can', 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', and above all 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now' — which was sitting there fully loaded, since the prospect had just confessed to a lifetime of making excuses for himself in exactly this area.

Trigger is real but soft — 'I don't just go around throwing $6,000 everywhere', plus reallocating against his gym membership and home projects. The isolation ran ('outside of splitting it up or how we specifically would pay it, do you feel like you do see yourself doing it?') and the rep used a decent reframe, that a painless price would produce no commitment. Beyond that, nothing: no financial picture at all, no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no investments, and no actual payment plan ever put on the table despite splitting being mentioned twice as theoretically available. The bigger issue is diagnostic — the prospect signalled clearly this was a value and allocation question rather than a capacity one, so the correct response was to build value against alternatives, not to hint at instalments.

Script gap, and the same one already logged from the Badrane Hriouch call: a cheaper alternative the prospect believes could work. Here it is the free DIY route — 'I could go online and say, hey, show me some kettlebell workouts, tell me what to eat' — reinforced by a trusted friend who trains professional athletes and sends him kettlebell advice for nothing. He also half-defeated it himself, twice, mentioning the sifting through content and the friend being too busy and in another country. Both concessions were available and neither was used. There is no play for defending a premium against a functioning free substitute, and this call needed one more than any other in the batch.

Second gap: an equipment and logistics blocker. He named it unprompted as one of his two main concerns before price was ever discussed — no kettlebells in the hotels and Latin American gyms he lives out of. The response was to suggest most gyms probably have one, admit not knowing, and hand the problem back: 'you're in sales, so you know how to do some problem solving.' The actual answer, that Trevor also programmes calisthenics and maces, emerged half an hour later in an unrelated exchange. The playbook has no step for confirming the prospect can physically execute the programme in their real environment, and for a fully remote product that is a structural omission.

Third gap: a stranger-danger and proof objection from a lead one day old. 'You guys right now, unfortunately, you're a stranger to me' at 00:18:05 went entirely unanswered; the related demand for detail at 00:35:00 was answered well, but only after the prospect pushed twice. This is the second call in this batch (with Edward Garcia) where a same-day or next-day lead needed evidence before spending thousands and there was no scripted route and nothing to send.
No partner or family in the decision, and none disclosed anywhere in the call.
No timing objection about life being too busy; his travel was raised as an execution constraint, not a reason to delay. The delay here is evaluative, which is OA territory and was handled there.
No fear or doubt about his own ability — he is a lifelong athlete and confident he can do the work. His doubt is about the vendor, not himself.

notes: This is the call to review with Richard. The prospect matches the stated ICP on every criterion, said outright that money was not the blocker, and still walked. Two causes, both fixable. He gave a price range of '$1,000 to $9,000' before finishing discovery because the prospect asked, then had to explain that the low end buys non-personalised programmes — disclosing a cheap tier and inviting the prospect to anchor there. And he left the two objections that actually mattered untouched: the free DIY alternative, and no kettlebells where this man actually lives. Both were raised by the prospect voluntarily and early. Hold the price until after the commitment check even under pressure, answer the equipment question with calisthenics and maces the moment it is asked, and go into the follow-up with something concrete to send — this buyer told you plainly that he needed to see what he was buying.
